description: Ordination hall of a wat, a rectangular pillared hall under steep multi-tiered roofs with horned gable finials and boundary stones at its corners.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Rectangular temple ordination hall under steeply pitched overlapping tiled roofs in three descending tiers, curved horn-shaped finials at each gable ridge end, carved triangular gable panel above the entrance, a colonnade of thick square columns around the outside supporting deep eaves, wide stepped entrance platform, small pointed boundary marker stones set at the corners Materials: Orange and green glazed roof tiles, gilded and mirror-inlaid gable carving dulled with dust, whitewashed stucco walls with damp staining at the base, red-lacquered columns worn at hand height, weathered grey boundary stones.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 13.90 x 16.92 x 24.00 m against the declared 14 x 17 x 24, the long axis on Z; band table against the Meshy proxy mean |delta width| 0.014, |delta depth| 0.029 of height (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs), from 0.017 / 0.044 in the second build. featureReviews.notes: Third build. The proxy side elevation was scanned column by column at 43 px/m (scratch/_mon/front.mjs): centre ridge 14.72 m over x 0..6, end ridges 13.84 m over x 6.1..8.9, the skirt hip 7.66 m at x 9.3 falling to 7.1 at x 10.2. So the top and middle registers were shortened from 17.9 to 17.0 m (bands 7-8 had read 0.08-0.10 H long), the end ridges lowered from 14.0 to 13.85, the skirt eaves raised from 6.9 to 7.2 with its hip top pulled in to z 7.8 for the shallow 27-degree end hips, and the columns carried to 6.9 m under the beam. The two residuals are reported rather than chased: band 7 width is gilt ornament the proxy cannot resolve, and band 4 depth is the raised skirt eaves now falling inside the band.

featureReviews.evidence: A hipped 37-degree portico skirt with 27-degree end hips, then a middle and a top register EACH telescoped into a 12 m centre and two 2.5 m ends (middle 9.0-10.85 / 8.65-10.5 m, top 10.9-14.8 / 10.55-13.85 m), every panel framed in glazed green on all four edges, gilt bargeboards, a stepped white gable fin at each telescope step, sixteen spiral horns and one carved pediment per end gable.
featureReviews.notes: The second build sectioned only the top register and read the proxy's continuous layer line as 'only the ridges step'; the plate's roof crop shows each end panel with its own green frame and a white step against the centre panel on the MIDDLE register too, so both registers are sectioned now and the centre gable slab carries the stepped outline (9.0 / 10.85 / 10.9 / 14.8). The green frame is the plate's clearest roof signal and the second build had it only at the eaves: it is now an eaves band, a top strip and a rake stripe per section end, one component at one draw call. Bargeboards went from white to gilt on the plate's lamyong; the horns from a sine arc that spiked to a ten-segment heading sweep 68 -> 118 degrees that curls back past vertical, the S-shaped chofa.

featureReviews.evidence: Thirty red columns at ONE draw call between white pedestals and capitals (a second InstancedMesh, 60 blocks at one draw call) under a red eaves beam at 6.55-7.15 m, a parapet between their bases, sixteen windows and two doors in stone surrounds, eight bai sema on the bottom terrace with one centred before each stair.
featureReviews.notes: Counted off the plate's right-hand elevation: eleven a side and four between the corners on each end. The plate's columns are red BETWEEN white blocks -- a pedestal continuous with the parapet and a capital under the beam -- and the second build's bare shafts to 6.6 m read as posts. Column tone was the other loss: #71332A rendered #5A2622 under its grime, near black against the plate's #8A5A4E; the third build probes the harness transfer on a flat bundle and authors the inverse, landing at #985847.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.735-0.860, each albedo authored as the inverse of a PROBED harness transfer so the RENDER lands on the plate: roof #CF8944 vs plate #CB8E64, green #6E6F51 vs #6D7052, columns #985847 vs #8A5A4E, lit platform luma 185 vs 176. Four Canvas 2D tiles: 18 x 12 laid tile course with 7% darker fired tiles and equal 1 px joints, streaked whitewash, four-flake peeling lacquer, kranok pediment on a dark lacquer ground. 4 textures, 5.3 MB, ~70 ms.
featureReviews.notes: The second build copied plate values onto the materials and rendered a beige platform, a tan roof and near-black columns: the harness's ACES output desaturates a lit 45-degree slope (a probe at #F2A262 came back #A58853), and a vertical face renders ~0.90x its authored value before the wear tile darkens it. The tile course was also a 1 m grid at 11 x 7 that read as graph paper, with wider vertical joints that read as bright stripes down every slope; the plate's crop counts ~18 tiles across 2.4 m. Stone washes were lightened and the red peel cut from six flakes to four so neither reads as blotches.

name: Ubosot
notes: The most sacred building of a wat and its visual anchor. Its identity is the roof: a wrap-around portico skirt, then a layered gable roof telescoped into three sections along the length -- the centre ridge higher than the two ends -- every slope broken into stepped layers with glazed eaves bands, white bargeboards and curved chofa horns at every apex and rake foot. The small pointed boundary marker stones at the corners are what make it an ordination hall specifically rather than a general assembly hall, so they belong to this asset and are not optional dressing. Declared 14 x 17 x 24 m: the 24 m length is correct for a full ordination hall, and the height and width were re-declared on 2026-08-26 from the Meshy proxy of the plate (long:h:short = 1 : 0.71 : 0.57), after the first build at 12 m tall read as squat against the reference. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.
